# stripe_country_spec (Data Source)

What Stripe supports in a country. Look one up by its `id`, the two-letter country code such as `US`. It omits `supported_bank_account_currencies`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "stripe_country_spec" "us" {
  id = "US"
}

output "us_default_currency" {
  value = data.stripe_country_spec.us.default_currency
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Optional

- `id` (String) Unique identifier for the object. Represented as the ISO country code for this country.

### Read-Only

- `default_currency` (String) The default currency for this country. This applies to both payment methods and bank accounts.
- `supported_payment_currencies` (List of String) Currencies that can be accepted in the specified country (for payments).
- `supported_payment_methods` (List of String) Payment methods available in the specified country. You may need to enable some payment methods (e.g., [ACH](https://stripe.com/docs/ach)) on your account before they appear in this list. The `stripe` payment method refers to [charging through your platform](https://stripe.com/docs/connect/destination-charges).
- `supported_transfer_countries` (List of String) Countries that can accept transfers from the specified country.
- `verification_fields` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--verification_fields))

<a id="nestedatt--verification_fields"></a>
### Nested Schema for `verification_fields`

Read-Only:

- `company` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--verification_fields--company))
- `individual` (Attributes) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--verification_fields--individual))

<a id="nestedatt--verification_fields--company"></a>
### Nested Schema for `verification_fields.company`

Read-Only:

- `additional` (List of String) Additional fields which are only required for some users.
- `minimum` (List of String) Fields which every account must eventually provide.
